we developed an efficient algorithm to detect and type high-risk HPV in FFPE specimens from cervical lesions and that we found HPV type distribution prior to HPV vaccine implementation.

the parallel testing algorithm yielded the highest HPV prevalence, the serial testing algorithm yielded a similar prevalence of HR types and the most common HPV types detected in invasive and pre-invasive cervical lesions were HPV16, 52, 31, and 33.

we developed a method for testing and reporting two commercial HPV assays on formalin fixed parffin embedded (FFFE) cervical specimens, and that the most common HPV types in invasive and pre-invasive cervical lesions were HPV16, 52, 33, 18 and 35.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of two different HPV DNA assays on the same sample is feasible.

the two assays were concordant for detection of high risk (HR) types, but the Linear Array was more sensitive for detecting low-risk (LR), and that the parallel algorithm detected more HPV types than the serial algorithm.
the parallel algorithm was more sensitive for detecting HPV, while the serial algorithm was more sensitive at detecting multiple HPV types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parallel algorithm, which is the most sensitive approach, should be used for testing HPV DNA in FFPE specimens.
HPV typing in FFPE samples can be performed using commercially available assays, but that the results may be affected by the algorithm used.
the two commercial HPV assays we tested are complementary and can be used to detect a wide range of HPV types in FFPE cervical specimens, including specimens with low DNA yield and poor quality.
